sections.heading: What's new in v0.10.0
sections.content: User notes now live outside the server repo at ~/.nutshell/notes — auto-updates can reset the daemon code without ever touching your data. Streaming chat is wired end-to-end: real Ollama / OpenRouter replies stream into the chat-prompt screen via lightweight container upgrades, with a per-session token-rate slider on the phone (dial to zero for an async 'thinking' animation that buffers and lands the full reply at once). Phone now renders the chat history above the textarea, scrolling stays in sync with which prompt the glasses are showing, and the chat-list nav doesn't grow ghost topics mid-stream. Container-name length cap (16 chars) caught us once — fixed and audited. This welcome note is refreshed from the server template on every restart so each release can drop a 'what's new' here. Edits revert; deletes return on next start; treat it as a release-notes channel, not a personal note.

sections.heading: What this is
sections.content: Nutshell turns anything you capture into a readable HUD view on your G2 glasses. The phone does the heavy lifting and the glasses just display.

sections.heading: Capture: URLs
sections.content: Paste a link into the URL box on the phone and tap Go. Nutshell fetches the page through Jina Reader, strips the clutter, and sends a clean summary with chapters to the glasses.

sections.heading: Capture: files and images
sections.content: Pick a .txt, .md, .pdf, or an image and tap Summarize. Text files and PDFs are summarized into chapters. Images are read via OCR so you can snap a page of a book or a slide and get a readable version on your glasses.

sections.heading: Capture: raw Markdown upload
sections.content: For .md files you can also tap Upload instead of Summarize. That skips the LLM and sends the file to the glasses verbatim. Headings that start with # become chapters and nested headings are indented under the top level so you can see the structure.

sections.heading: Reading on the glasses
sections.content: The launch surface is the root menu: time on the left, a chat / notes list on the right. Scroll to highlight, tap to enter; double-tap exits the app. From notes, the home screen is your projects + saved notes newest first. From chat, you land on a sessions picker, then a session opens the chat surface.

sections.heading: Chat: streaming, sessions, history
sections.content: Pick or create a session on the phone. Type a prompt, hit send. The reply streams live onto the glasses prompt view as well as into the phone's chat history pane. Scroll past the bottom of one prompt to advance into the next; double-tap to walk back up the chain. Token rate is a per-session knob so you can tune how fast the text paints — zero turns it into batch mode.

sections.heading: Ask: voice questions
sections.content: While reading a note you can ask a voice question about it. The Ask view is a half-screen bordered overlay that drops in at the top of the reading page. The reading text stays visible in the bottom half behind it. Hold for at least a second, then single tap to send, or double tap to dismiss. The answer replaces Listening in the same overlay so you never lose your place.

sections.heading: QA Bank: every answer is saved
sections.content: Every successful question is saved on the current note forever and shown in a half-screen list at the bottom of the reading page. A pending entry is written the moment you send so dismissing mid-flight still records the question. The answer and a short rewritten title fill in automatically when the model finishes.

sections.heading: Errors are ephemeral
sections.content: If the model is unreachable, your API key is wrong, or your utterance was too short, the QA Bank will show a short ERROR entry telling you what went wrong. These entries are not kept forever. The next time you open Nutshell, all error entries and any Ask that was still in flight when you closed the app are dropped.

sections.heading: Head gestures: look up and look down
sections.content: While reading you can look up to open Ask hands free and look down to open the QA Bank for the current note. Both are off by default. Turn them on in Settings and run the one time Calibrate flow so the detector learns which axis is pitch on your head. Gestures only fire while you are reading so they never interrupt other screens.

sections.heading: Notes management
sections.content: Every note you save persists across app restarts, including your OpenRouter API key and your saved QA Bank entries. On the phone you can export a single note to Markdown, export all notes at once, or delete individual notes.

sections.heading: Settings and API key
sections.content: Open the Settings tab on the phone to paste your OpenRouter API key, toggle head gestures, run gesture calibration, and tune the glasses layout knobs. A live Glasses Status panel shows the bridge state, current screen, current note, current chapter, and the last API call.
